import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Filter for the latest available StichtagDatJahr to get the most recent snapshot of data.
# This avoids counting the same dog multiple times across different annual snapshots.
latest_year = df['StichtagDatJahr'].max()
df_latest = df[df['StichtagDatJahr'] == latest_year].copy()

# Set a visually appealing style for the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a figure and a set of subplots to display multiple insights
fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(12, 20))
fig.suptitle(f'Zurich Dog Registration Data - Snapshot {latest_year}', fontsize=18, y=1.02, weight='bold')

# --- Plot 1: Top 10 Most Common Dog Breeds ---
# Count primary breeds, excluding 'Mischling' (mixed breed) and 'Unbekannt' (unknown)
# to focus on specific breed popularity.
top_breeds = df_latest[~df_latest['Rasse1Text'].isin(['Mischling', 'Unbekannt'])]['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().head(10)
sns.barplot(x=top_breeds.values, y=top_breeds.index, ax=axes[0], palette='viridis')
axes[0].set_title('Top 10 Most Common Dog Breeds (Excluding Mixed/Unknown)', fontsize=15)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Breed', fontsize=12)
axes[0].tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=10)
axes[0].tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=10)
axes[0].bar_label(axes[0].containers[0], fmt='%.0f', padding=5, fontsize=9) # Add labels to bars

# --- Plot 2: Dog Distribution Across Districts ---
# Count dogs per district and sort them by district name for better readability.
district_counts = df_latest['KreisLang'].value_counts().sort_index()
sns.barplot(x=district_counts.values, y=district_counts.index, ax=axes[1], palette='plasma')
axes[1].set_title('Dog Distribution Across Zurich Districts', fontsize=15)
axes[1].set_xlabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('District', fontsize=12)
axes[1].tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=10)
axes[1].tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=10)
axes[1].bar_label(axes[1].containers[0], fmt='%.0f', padding=5, fontsize=9)

# --- Plot 3: Dog Age Distribution ---
# Use 'AlterVHundNum' (numerical age of the dog in years) to create a histogram.
# Ensure age is non-negative and handle potential missing values if any.
ages = df_latest['AlterVHundNum'].dropna()
sns.histplot(ages, bins=range(0, int(ages.max()) + 2), kde=False, ax=axes[2], color='skyblue', edgecolor='black')
axes[2].set_title('Distribution of Dog Ages', fontsize=15)
axes[2].set_xlabel('Age (Years)', fontsize=12)
axes[2].set_ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=12)
# Set x-ticks to show every 2 years for better readability, up to the max age
axes[2].set_xticks(range(0, int(ages.max()) + 1, 2))
axes[2].tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=10)
axes[2].tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=10)

# Adjust layout to prevent titles and labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.98])

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
